Your next customer isn't human. It's their agent.
That was the title of Kai-Thomas Krause’s (@kaithomaskrause) talk at AI:Deep Dive Berlin this week, and he showed it live on stage.

A shopping agent is a strange customer. It sees none of the design you built over the last 20 years, it reads your product pages and return policy in seconds, and it does so in many shops at once. If your shop can’t deliver an answer, it doesn’t wait. It buys somewhere else.

Three things from the talk:
1️⃣ Personal agents are the next wave. Meta Muse passed 10 million users within weeks, and Instinct already works in Germany. Kai regularly buys from a German shop with it.

2️⃣ Today these agents click through shops in a virtual browser, pretending to be human. In the live demo that took about 2.5 minutes for one purchase. The same kind of request over the Personal Agent Protocol, where the agent identifies itself and the merchant decides what it may do, took seconds.

3️⃣ Shops aren’t ready. We tested 50 DACH fashion shops: none supports the Personal Agent Protocol, only 2 support UCP discovery, 36% deliver no usable product page without JavaScript, and 14% block every non-browser client.

We are turning this into the Agentic Leadership Report: 100 shops in Europe, 100 in DACH and 100 German fashion shops, measured repeatedly so the trend becomes visible. It will be out in the next few weeks. https://t.co/tNZcCcqi6Q

Kai’s advice for brands and retailers: block, open up or build your own agent. Any of these can be right, as long as there is a strategy behind it. Doing nothing is the worst one.

Thanks to team one (especially Paul Krauss) for a great evening and to @stripe for hosting.

#AgenticCommerce #Ecommerce #AIAgents #Retail

1 | Shopee delivered another quarter of strong growth, continue to see long growth runway and expect unit economics to keep improving. Expect FY26 GMV growth of 25% and Adj EBITDA of $1bn.

Shopee delivered another quarter of strong growth while generating the highest quarterly profit we have ever achieved. Our strategies have proven effective at strengthening our fundamentals, giving us a growing buyer base, stronger monetization and improving unit economics. We still see a long runway of opportunity ahead, and we will keep executing with the discipline to capture it. We remain on track to deliver GMV growth of around 25% and an adjusted EBITDA of $1 billion for the full year of 2026.

2 | Shopee saw strong acceleration in new user growth, driving strong growth in active buyers.

The acceleration in new user growth we saw in the second quarter has continued into the third. We engaged and reengaged a broad range of user through both online and offline campaigns, brought our content to more social and video platforms and widened our service options, especially in delivery to serve different user needs. With these efforts, new average monthly active buyers grew more than 50% and the total average monthly active buyers increased by 20% YoY.

3 | Ecommerce monetization also doing well, driven by ads, where ad-paying sellers grew 35%, ad revenue grew 55% and ad-take rates rose 80bps.

Monetization has also continued to do well, driven by ads. Sellers are responding well to the greater value they see in our AI-driven ad solutions. Ad paying sellers rose more than 35% while average asset per seller increased around 13% YoY, and revenue grew more than 55% and our ad take-rate improved by over 80bps YoY.

4 | Expect Shopee monetization to improve, primarily coming from higher-margin advertising and to flow to growing EBITDA.

We expect going forward, our monetization will also be better, primarily from the ad side, less from the xed commission side. And part of that will ow to the bottom line EBITDA improvement over time. And part of that might go to the investment to grow our market further as well.

5 | Continued logistics improvements is allowing Shopee to serve a wider range of buyer needs from instant, same day to low cost services.

Our operational priorities to enhance service quality, price competitiveness and the discovery remain consistent and continue to be driven by our efforts in Logistics, ShopeeVIP and our content ecosystem. Each made good progress this quarter. First, Logistics. We expected our delivery options to serve a wider range of buyer needs from instant and same-day delivery to low-cost services. Our instant delivery service can now deliver as quickly as 1 hour. This has expanded our addressable market by unlocking new spending scenarios where speed matters most. These tend to be high-frequency categories such as the growth rate and the pharmaceutical items, boosting our overall purchase frequency.

6 | Strong traction in Indonesia and Thailand, orders in Indonesia 2X, same day delivery now 15% of orders in Bangkok.

In Indonesia, orders using the services more than doubled YoY, with cost per order declining year-on-year. Retailer share have increased the service. We now have more than 12,000 offline stores on our instant platform and growing.

Adoption is also growing in Thailand, where instant and same-day delivery rate now account for nearly 15% of orders in Greater Bangkok. We will continue to grow this service in areas where demand is high and the unit economics make sense.

7 | Buyer self-collection reached 30% in Singapore and 15% in Malaysia, which is a much cheap shipping option.

In the third quarter, buyer self-collection order penetration reached more than 30% in Singapore and more than 15% in Malaysia. In Indonesia, our economical shipping option has gained strong adoption and now accounts for more than half of total orders. This cost of order is more than 20% lower than the platform average in the market. These initiatives allowed us to offer free shipping at a lower minimum spend, giving our buyers the exibility to choose between cost and speed and letting us serve a broader range of buyers' needs.

8 | Shopee remains focused on scaling fulfilment quickly, orders grew 25% QoQ, unit economics improving, parcels delivered next day or sooner grew twice as fast as overall growth.

We have also continued to scale fulfillment quickly. Sellers have responded well to our fulfillment offerings as we help them take on the complexity of storing, packing and shipping. This represents significant efficiency gains for them, especially during peak campaign period where orders may be several times higher than normal. With our services, sellers can build their businesses more easily without having to increase their own warehouse space or staff size. In the third quarter, fulflled order volumes accelerated to around 25% QoQ. Unit economics for our fulfilled by Shopee service improved sequentially in Asia, and we see further room to gain efficiency through higher warehouse utilization and automation. Fulfillment also drives synergies with delivery, enabling us to deliver more packages more quickly. The number of parcels delivered by the next day or sooner grew over 16% YoY, more than twice as fast as our overall order growth.

9 | ShopeeVIP continues to grow rapidly, hitting 21m +40% QoQ, and members now account for 25% of Shopee’s overall GMV, and have higher monthly retention of 80%, and spend more.

ShopeeVIP is growing fast. Membership across markets exceeded 21 million at the end of September, up more than 40% quarter-on-quarter and members contributed close to 25% of Shopee's overall GMV. The program is demonstrating stickiness with monthly retention around 80%. Members show a consistent double-digit percentage uplift in spend on average after subscribing. And with more sellers and partners investing alongside us in membership benefits, the program's unit economics improved sequentially.

10 | Orders from live streaming and short-form video grew 45% and now account for 25% of physical good orders in SEA.

Orders from live streaming and short-form video grew more than 45% YoY and accounted for more than 25% of physical goods orders in Southeast Asia. Unit economics also improved sequentially. Beyond our app, our a liate program remains an effective and growing channel to bring new buyers to Shopee from other platforms.

11 | Content business is profit margin accretive rather than dilutive.

For content ecosystem, which includes video live stream, I think it's a bit hard to split a particular segment to the EBITDA level because there are many shared costs below that. I think for us, we look at sort of variable cost or contribution margins to our platform, the content platform that has a positive contribution margin. Essentially, what we're saying is if we grow content business more in our platforms, we'll have more profit rather than has less profit for our businesses.

12 | Social media orders from YouTube, Facebook, and Instagram grew rapidly from affiliate creators.

In the third quarter, orders driven by YouTube content more than doubled YoY and Shopee affiliate orders generated by Facebook linked creators grew more than 90% QoQ. On Instagram, more than 4 million reels have been tagged with Shopee products since we launched the partnership in April with the number growing more than 4x QoQ.

13 | Shopee is one of the few ecommerce platforms that is open to agents with Meta Muse, while still early, expect it to become a solid channel for buyer acquisition and GMV growth.

Shopee is also one of the early connector partners for Meta's Muse AI personal assistant that has just launched in Singapore. Users will be able to research and compare products on Shopee through Muse, helping them make purchase decisions tailored to their preferences. The partnership is still at an early stage, but we see potential for it to become a solid additional channel for buyer acquisition and incremental GMV growth over time.

14 | Open to working with agents, because checkout, seller and buyer relationships still remain with Shopee.

Coming to the second question on the agentic AI, we actually partnered with a range of partners starting from ChatGPT and now as you mentioned, the Muse. At this point in time, all the checkout and seller relationships and buyer relationships happen within the Shopee platform. And we didn't see a meaningful impact to our economics for the near future.

15 | Brazil remains the fastest-growing for Shopee, and grew faster than the broader market, gaining share, and continue to improve buyer waiting time by 12%.

Brazil remains our fastest-growing market, and we again grew faster than the broader market in the third quarter. Logistics improvements underpinned this growth. We continue to widen the range of faster delivery options we offer across the country with average buyer waiting time improving 12% YoY. We have branched into air delivery, cutting delivery times to the North and the Northeast regions significantly.

16 | In São Paulo, ~40% of parcels now arrive next days do 60% within 2 days, stronger delivery capabilities is adding more sellers to Shopee in Brazil

In Greater Sao Paulo, around 40% of parcels now arrive at the next day and nearly 60% within 2 days. Our new instant delivery service there, Shopee Turbo already delivers in under 4 hours from more than 7,000 partner stores. Stronger delivery capabilities have enabled us to onboard more sellers to fulfillment.

17 | This is allowing Shopee to expand beyond smaller-item ecommerce to more expensive and larger items into more upmarket buyer segments and higher value categories, and with Shopee Mall, which is where MELI dominates.

For example, we rolled out an in-house delivery service for bulky items such as the large appliances and furniture, combined with our strong service reputation and reliable cross nation coverage. This has made more large item sellers willing to ful ll with us.

Across the country, fulfillment order volume more than doubled YoY. These service quality improvements have helped drive stronger growth in higher-value categories. More upmarket buyers are joining Shopee and existing buyers are shopping across more categories with us. Automotive and home improvement categories grew more than 80% yearon-year and more brand sellers have come on board.

Shopee Mall orders carried an average basket size, almost 3x the platform average. Looking ahead, we see a lot of headroom to grow in this exciting market.

18 | Don’t see a meaningful growth deceleration for Shopee GMV yet, but noticed more value-seeking ecommerce buying behaviour.

On the Shopee growth, first of all, we don't see a big Shopee GMV growth rate slowdown yet. As we shared earlier, in Q3, we do see a meaningful growth, similar growth rate compared to last quarter from a year-to-year perspective, if we take away the ForEx impact. You are right that there are many macro factors like fuel price, et cetera, impacting the consumption.

Overall, we see that although we have noticed some more value-seeking behaviors in our market due to all this macro environment, but the general overall demand is relatively resistant.

19 | Shopee is well positioned as they are focused on long-tail products with competitive pricing that positions them better with people who need to buy rather than impulse buying. Still see long growth runway in e-commerce.

But again, I would like to reiterate that our competitive advantage will continue to differentiate us from the peers even in the macro situation that we are in right now, given that we are -- we built our platform around long-tail products and also the pricing in our platform is a lot more competitive compared to other platforms online or compared to the alternative offline as well. On top of that, many of our -- large part of our platform's GMV are driven by the people who have the need to purchase rather than people who have impulse buying. All those make us -- put us in a more resistance position on the growth for our e-commerce in our market. I think we will continue to monitor our market very closely for any changes. But again, given all the things we mentioned above, and also the e-commerce penetration are still relatively low compared to many other markets, we still believe that there is a big runway for us to grow our e-commerce in the regions.

20 | Monee has grown beyond its original origins of payments into mobile wallet, credit, and digitial banking, and is growing fast and very profitable.

Monee has grown well beyond its origins as a payment infrastructure serving our internal business needs. Today, it has evolved into a financial services business across mobile wallet, credit, digital banking and more. Monee has shown consistent strong growth and has been profitable for the last 3 fiscal years.

21 | Monee has reached the scale and maturity to benefit from becoming independent, and a standalone public listing in the coming 1-3 years will make sense.

We believe Monee has reached the scale and maturity to extend itself and would benefit from becoming more independent…Our ambition is to keep growing Monee into a full financial ecosystem with inclusion at its heart, serving users across their life cycle needs from unsecured loans to secured lending, insurance, wealth management and more. We believe a stand-alone listing would give Monee the dedicated capital base it needs to build this ecosystem and let it invest for growth while managing risk with discipline.

We hope to list the Monee at the right time in the next 1 to 3 years, taking into consideration factors such as market conditions, macro environment and regulatory requirements.

22 | Monee and Shopee will continue to work together, and remain a key payment and credit partner for Shopee, and insights from Shopee used to drive Monee.

I want to be clear about what does not change. Monee and Shopee will continue to work closely together as they do today. Monee will remain a key payment and credit partner for Shopee and Shopee will remain a key platform for Monee to reach users. Insights from our businesses will continue to empower Monee's growth.

23 | BNPL is growing rapidly, driving faster growth in Shopee’s SPayLater portfolio >2X, and is now 25% overall and nearly 40% in Malaysia.

As pay later is becoming an everyday way to pay both online and offine in many of our markets, our off-Shopee SPayLater portfolio more than doubled year-on-year to nearly 25% of our entire SPayLater portfolio at the end of September. In Malaysia, its share is nearly 40%. In Thailand, the ShopeePay unlimited cards allows SPayLater users to accept their approved SPayLater credit limit wherever Mastercard is accepted.

24 | Risk management remains top priority for Monee, 90 day NPL ratio inched up small to 1.3%. Continue to proactively adjust underwriting criteria depending on macro.

Risk management remains our top priority as we continue to grow our loan book. Our 90-day NPL ratio was 1.3% at the end of September. The modest uptick primarily reects an evolving credit environment, especially in Thailand and Brazil as well as market and product mix, including faster growth in Brazil in o-Shopee SPayLater. Our underwriting is highly responsive to market conditions. We proactively adjusted our underwriting criteria and credit limit management for selected customer segments at early signs of softness to maintain disciplined growth and optimize risk-adjusted returns. We are staying close to the data and we'll keep adjusting as needed. So our loan book growth stays healthy and sustainable.

25 | Garena grew bookings LSD despite strong comps with improving profitability.

Garena delivered a solid third quarter with bookings continuing to grow from the high base set last year. Profitability also improved. Free Fire anchored this performance with a strong bookings growth and Arena of Valor continued its strong momentum from its 10th year anniversary celebrations.

26 | Setting up Sea Cloud as a frugal start-up, not seeking to own large amounts of physical capacity, only for customers with dedicated computing capacity, and pursue with clear customer commitments and attractive returns.

We are setting up Sea Cloud as a frugal start-up so that it can stay nimble and respond quickly to market demand. Our focus is the software and customer relationships, not owning large amounts of physical capacity, where customers need dedicated computing capacity, we will only pursue opportunities with clear customer commitments and attractive returns. We will mainly look to partners and customer prepayments to fund the physical infrastructure.

27 | Still early, do not expect Sea Cloud to have a significant impact on financials, they still figuring out. Probably work better for their SMB merchants than the AI labs or the enterprises which is what the hyperscalers focus on.

As a result, we do not expect Sea Cloud to have a significant impact on our financials for now. It is still early, and we will update investors on any meaningful developments.

So that is kind of the big picture we are looking at, and we think the demand will be huge, and this is just at a very, very early stage. So we want to get into this business early. There's a lot of things we don't know yet. And again, this is very early. This is kind of a start-up. So there's a lot of things we need to gure out, for example, what exactly the segment we should focus on, what exactly type of customers we should focus on and what is the best business model we should use. We think we'll get a better picture when we really get into the -- get our own feet into the game and we start to get the rst-hand experience.

28 | Sea Cloud has not secured any enterprise contracts yet, will primarily buy GPUs (as don’t have own chips). Expect the business to be more deal driven than its current businesses.

Sea Cloud, for your question, as you know, this is just at the very, very beginning of the business. At this moment, we don't have any -- we haven't secured any enterprise contracts. And for the investment in the data center and the GPUs, we -- let me put it in this way, we denitely probably will invest in the GPUs primarily for our own use. So regardless if there is a Sea Cloud business or not, like how the business progress down the road, we are going to invest into GPUs and primarily for all the internal use cases.
But the business nature is a bit di erent from the Sea Cloud. I think it will be very much deal by deal driven, at least at the beginning stage and with very, very speci c target in terms of the custom

29 | Another strong quarter across all three businesses with solid growth momentum, operational efficiency, and improving profitability.

In conclusion, we have delivered another strong quarter. Our 3 businesses have all expanded their addressable opportunity and strengthened their competitive position. Unit economics continue to improve across many of our initiatives, a testament to our financial discipline and operational efficiency. Our positive momentum across the rst 3 quarters give us greater condence for the rest of the year.

➡️ Key takeaways on Sea Limited: SEA’s most dominant ecommerce platform with Shopee and increasingly its logistics fulfilment platform SPX and its credit lending business Monee riding on Shopee. Garena continues to recover and provides the reinvestment ability to double down. Continue to see a long runway of growth opportunity, and not concerned over the near-term higher investments weighing on near-term profitability, which are beneficial for longer term growth and profitability. Valuations remain undemanding and attractive.

Grok Bot vs Claude Duet:

Grok Bot is built for the heavy stuff, enterprise use, multi-agent coordination. You train an agent on a specific job, then drop it into a group with others. They work together on multi-step workflows, hand things off, and keep moving even when you're offline. Sales follow-ups, expense checks, recruiting runs, ops that used to eat whole afternoons. It feels like staffing a small team that already knows your tools. Its highly addicting and we see it as the clear winner as a business solution.

Duet is different. If you already live in Claude and have all your context in-platforn, it can act more like a personal assistant that notices things. Morning briefs, spotting stuff that needs a look, drafting based on what it already knows about how you work. It tries to be proactive instead of waiting for a prompt every time.

I tried the Duet preview. It was okay, but not that useful yet. The model underneath didn't feel as smart as Opus 5.5. The proactive parts weren't helpful for me, and a lot of the time it still needed me to point it in the right direction. It felt much less capable than GrokBot. Once it leaves preview and gets a real launch I expect it to improve a lot, especially for people who are already deep Claude users.

Right now it is Duet feels like more of an assistant for technical people who want Claude watching their day than a platform for coordinating multiple agents. We say that its just like Meta Muse but built for AI dorks.

Which one are you leaning toward?
